newsitem.title: UK: Cargo MEDIA details 1997 EDI items, start dates.
newsitem.headline: Cargo MEDIA details 1997 EDI items, start dates.

text.p: The 18 member airlines of the Cargo Multinational EDI Association (Cargo MEDIA) have agreed dates in 1997 for the implementation for key airfreight electronic data interchange(EDI) items, the association said in a statement.
These include the implementation of an EDI based reservations facility, a neutral air waybill and four priority status messages, it added

Cargo Media chairman, Robert Cutler from Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said the outcome "was a significant achievement by the group and confirms the commitment of its members in meeting their customer requirements in a quality and timely manner."

The agreement came during Cargo Media's board meeting in Paris in mid-September. The airlines also agreed to consider setting up in each of their home markets, an EDI implementation group to promote and develop such messaging, the statement said.
The first group has been set up in the UK and will be chaired by British Airways Plc, while a similar group will be formed in the U.S. and be chaired by Northwest Airlines.
In detail the following measures(Schedule One) will start on January 1,1997.
*Use of an EDI reservations facility, enabling customers to make bookings electronically with member airlines.
*Introduction of the four priority status messages on which the group has been working. These are
*consignments departed on a given flight(DEP)
*consignments delivered to consignee (DLV)
*consignments transferred to another airline or transport
company (TFD).
Most members will also introduce the discrepancy(DIS) message for missing cargo(MSCA), found cargo(FDCA) and offloaded cargo (OFLD) by the same date, it added .
The remaining members will implement these no later than 30th June 1997.

All member airlines confirmed that they would use the IATA Edition 14 Version 6 of the air waybill message (FWB) as a minimum with effect from January 1, 1997. They also agreed to support the introduction of the neutral air waybill in all markets.
The statement said the Paris meeting also reviewed other messages (Schedule Two) and confirmed their implementation from end-1997. These are
*consignment received from shipper or forwarder (RCS),
*consignment received from flight(RCF)
*consignment received from another airline(RCT)
*consignment booked or rebooked (BKD)
*consignment cleared customs(CCD) as well as the discrepancy messages for consignment short shipped (SPPD) and consignment overloaded (OVLD).

A bar code labelling implementation programme will be prepared for the group by March 1997, for consideration by each member with a view to the introduction of bar code technology at all member-served airports at home and overseas, it added.

To ensure consistency in the application of bar code label procedure in the industry, representatives of all member airlines will meet in the near future for a seminar on the subject, the statement said.
Cargo MEDIA was formed in 1995 to promote EDI amongst in the airfreight industry and it says its members now handle 75 percent of the world's scheduled international air cargo.

Apart from the airlines mentioned above, Cargo MEDIA members are Aer Lingus, Air Canada, Air France, Alitalia , American Airlines, Austrian Airlines, Japan Airlines, KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV, Korean Airlines, Deutsche Lufthansa AG, Qantas SAS, Singapore Airlines, Swissair and United Airlines. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
